The simulation uses the twoPhaseEulerFoam solver for a steady-state, two-phase (oil-water) flow in a horizontal pipe.
The pipe is oriented along the x-axis with a diameter of 0.1 m and a length of 2 m.
The computational domain is a cylindrical pipe represented by a structured hexahedral mesh with approximately 200 cells along the length, 20 cells across the diameter, and 1 cell in the third direction.
The inlet boundary is at x = 0 m and the outlet boundary is at x = 2 m.
The pipe wall is a noSlip boundary for the velocity field and a zeroGradient boundary for alpha.water.
Gravity is set to (0, -9.81, 0) m/s², acting perpendicular to the pipe axis in the negative y-direction.
The mixture velocity U at the inlet is fixedValue with value uniform (0.5 0 0).
The mixture velocity U at the outlet is inletOutlet.
The static pressure p at the outlet is fixedValue with value uniform 0.
The static pressure p at the inlet is inletlet.
In 0/alpha.water, the inlet boundary is fixedValue with value uniform 0.3.
In 0/alpha.water, the outlet boundary is fixedValue with value uniform 0.3.
The water phase has a density of 1000 kg/m³ and a kinematic viscosity of 1e-6 m²/s.
The oil phase has a density of 850 kg/m³ and a kinematic viscosity of 0.001 m²/s.
The simulation is run as a transient calculation with a time step of 0.001 s and continued until the field residuals converge to a steady state.
The PIMPLE algorithm is used with 2 outer correctors and 2 pressure correctors per time step.
